Category.reason: Confirmed. The data are UK Biobank population-cohort data: Oxford WebQ 24-h dietary recalls (choline estimated from the USDA food-composition database), hospital and death-record ICD-9/10 codes for incident dementia/AD/MCI, touchscreen cognitive tests, and questionnaire covariates. No CSF, plasma, genomic or omic data are analysed. The limitations say genotypes were not available ('due to the absence of genetic data, we included the family history of dementia as a covariate instead of specific genotypes', p.7), and circulating choline was not measured (p.8). So C3 has no basis as a data domain, and the primary domain, C5, is missing. That choline is a molecule describes the exposure, not the data domain.
